title: HINT for Procurement — RFPs stay vendor-neutral
metaDescription: Keep requirements, sources, timelines, evaluation rules and internal scoring separate so assistants draft fair procurement documents.
h1: Your assistant drafts RFPs fast. HINT keeps them fair and source-based.
intro: HINT keeps requirements, timelines, evaluation rules and approvals in plain-text notes beside tender documents. Your assistant reads the rules for this procurement before drafting supplier-facing language.

situations.before: An RFP requirement happens to describe one vendor's product.
situations.body: Brand-specific language must have an approved source or be rewritten around the business need.

situations.before: Internal evaluation weights leak into the supplier document.
situations.after: Scoring stays in its proper boundary
situations.body: Internal evaluation context is available to the panel without being emitted into the RFP.

situations.before: A budget figure appears because the assistant assumed a range.
situations.body: Missing budgets and deadlines become questions for the procurement owner rather than invented commitments.

example.intro: The Springfield procurement demo grounds an evaluation requirement in SRC-1.
example.after: It writes neutral evaluation language grounded in the approved source and keeps internal scoring details out of supplier-facing material.
example.compiled:
<requirement name="overview-1">
  Approved requirement grounded in SRC-1.
</requirement>
<source name="SRC-1">../../sources/approved.md</source>

never: Invent a budget, deadline, approval or vendor fact.
Write a brand-specific requirement without a justified source.
Expose confidential evaluation weights in the RFP.
disclaimer: HINT assists with procurement documentation; your policies, legal review and delegated authority govern the actual process and award.

faq.a: No. It keeps criteria and evidence structured; authorized evaluators make and approve the decision.
Declare outcome-based requirements and prohibit unsupported brand references; reviewers still assess legitimate exceptions.
Only if your declared evaluation policy says so. HINT does not invent a scoring rule.

keywordDescriptions.tender: Sets the procurement, authority and document boundary.
keywordDescriptions.need: States the business outcome behind the purchase.
keywordDescriptions.requirement: States a supplier-facing need with a stable identifier.
keywordDescriptions.budget: Records an authorized budget from a named source.
keywordDescriptions.criterion: Names a factor evaluators apply consistently.
keywordDescriptions.weight: Records confidential scoring importance where authorized.
keywordDescriptions.exclusion: Marks an internal rule that must not enter the RFP.
keywordDescriptions.question: Records an approved supplier clarification.
